results.name: The Claim You Deserve: Denied & Underpaid Home Insurance Claim Corpus
results.what_gives_it_away_free: uphelp.org (United Policyholders) [VERIFIED, fetched uphelp.org/claim-guidance-publications/sample-letters-and-examples/, HTTP 200]: 20 sample claim-communication letters (policy copy request, ALE extension, contents itemization waiver, denial-info request, mortgage-release, code-upgrade benefits — two of these state-specific to CA), plus expense-tracking spreadsheets and damage-report resources. Confirmed absent from that library: no appraisal-demand letters, no 50-state statute/deadline matrix, no matching/line-of-sight bulletin compilation. It is prose coaching plus generic letters, not a normalized, cited, 50-state dataset. Nolo: searched, found only a free legal-encyclopedia article 'Handling Homeowners' Insurance Claims' (fetch blocked, HTTP 402/anti-bot) — no dedicated Nolo book on this exact niche surfaced, unlike the trademark and estate-executor niches.
results.what_exists: Etsy: 'Pre Existing Damage Insurance Claim Appeal Letter Template | Homeowners Denial Response | Property Claim Help' (editable letter + PDF + clause bank + instructions) [VERIFIED, search result, price not fetched]. No AI-corpus, prompt-pack, or 'Claude/GPT skill' product for home-insurance claims found on Gumroad or Etsy in targeted searches [VERIFIED-negative]. ClaimBack.app confirmed free but explicitly medical/health-only, no home coverage [carried from source doc, VERIFIED].
results.prompt_test_result: Tried the reasoning directly: given 'here is my denial letter and policy, what are my rights in Texas and draft an appraisal demand,' a strong model today produces a fluent, structurally correct appraisal/bad-faith explainer (this concept is well represented in training data) but has no reliable way to reproduce a specific state's insurer-response deadline citation or, especially, a state matching/line-of-sight bulletin (e.g., whether discontinued shingles force full-slope replacement) — these are buried DOI PDFs, not commonly discussed prose, and a model asked for one will confidently invent a plausible-sounding rule or citation number. That specific failure mode (matching-bulletin fabrication) is the corpus's strongest defensible square inch; the general appraisal/bad-faith framework is not defensible on its own.

results.name: Seized at the Border: the CBP Cash & Goods Seizure Response Corpus
results.what_gives_it_away_free: CBP itself supplies only bare forms (4609/4630) [carried, VERIFIED in source doc]. Great Lakes Customs Law fetched directly [VERIFIED, HTTP 200, greatlakescustomslaw.com/customs-money-seizure/]: confirmed to be lead-generation only — no specific deadlines, no mitigation-percentage tables, no sample petition language, no FP&F directory; it explains concepts then drives to 'Schedule Consultation.' No nonprofit or regulator publishes the mitigation-guideline percentage bands or an FP&F office directory for free. Nolo: searched, found no Nolo title on customs cash seizure/forfeiture [VERIFIED-negative search].
results.what_exists: No DIY kit, AI pack, or template product found on Gumroad, Etsy, or the open web for CBP/CAFRA seizure response in targeted searches [VERIFIED-negative]. The only competitors identified are $3,500+ law firms (Great Lakes, National Security Law Firm, etc.), consistent with the source doc's claim.
results.prompt_test_result: A good model given a seizure notice will correctly explain the general CAFRA/petition-vs-claim framework (well-represented in training data as a legal concept) but cannot supply the actual mitigation remission percentage bands FDA/CBP applies by violation type — it will either refuse to guess or invent plausible-sounding percentages, and it has no access to current port-specific FP&F filing addresses. In a domain where checking the wrong Election-of-Proceedings box forfeits five figures irreversibly, this is a genuine, high-stakes hallucination gap the corpus closes.
results.evidence: [VERIFIED] Google autocomplete fetched for 'CBP seized my cash' returned that exact phrase as a top suggestion (weak signal — tool returned a single suggestion, not a rich list, so demand breadth is not strongly confirmed this session). [VERIFIED] greatlakescustomslaw.com fetched HTTP 200, confirmed lead-gen-only content. [VERIFIED, from source doc, re-confirmed via search] a real law-firm content ecosystem around 'election of proceedings,' 'petitions vs claims for cash seized by CBP,' and 'abandoning cash to CBP' exists (greatlakescustomslaw.com, nationalsecuritylawfirm.com) — such content is not produced for unsearched terms. [UNKNOWN] precise monthly case volume; cbp.gov stats dashboard still returns 403 to direct fetch, so the ~26/month target-vs-pool arithmetic remains unverified this session, same as the source doc flagged.

results.name: Office Action Answer Kit
results.what_gives_it_away_free: USPTO's own page fetched directly [VERIFIED, uspto.gov/trademarks/maintain/responding-office-actions, HTTP 200]: confirmed general procedure and deadlines only, explicitly no sample response arguments, no template language, no worked examples — it tells applicants to 'make specific, fact-based points' without ever showing one. BUT: Nolo sells 'Trademark: Legal Care for Your Business & Product Name' at ~$30 [VERIFIED price via Walmart/AbeBooks listings], and a third-party review states it 'includes real-world examples of amendments... and office actions' [PLAUSIBLE, diylegalproducts.com summary via search, book itself not directly fetched — Nolo's own site returned HTTP 402/anti-bot to direct fetch]. This is the same Nolo-at-$14-43 pattern that killed the estate-executor candidate, so it is flagged as a real, not hypothetical, risk — though this book covers the whole trademark-filing lifecycle with office actions as one chapter, not a specialized 150-300-response, citation-verified corpus for substantive 2(d)/descriptiveness refusals.
results.what_exists: ActionResponder.ai fetched directly [VERIFIED, HTTP 200]: confirmed built for trademark professionals/attorneys and law-practice workflows, not individual pro se filers; no consumer tier, no public pricing, uses 'real citations' and 'curated exhibits' language that validates the corpus thesis but does not compete for this buyer. Questel and TrademarKraft are similar attorney-facing AI tools [VERIFIED as existing via search]. No Etsy or Gumroad office-action AI template/prompt-pack product found in targeted searches [VERIFIED-negative].
results.prompt_test_result: Asking a good model to 'draft a complete response to my Section 2(d) refusal with case citations' produces fluent structure and correct legal factors (du Pont factors etc. are well represented in training data) but the case citations it supplies cannot be trusted without independent verification — fabricated or misattributed legal citations are a well-documented LLM failure mode in exactly this kind of drafting task [PLAUSIBLE, not re-tested live this session, but the class of failure is well established]. The model also has no way to know current fees/deadlines precisely (the 3-month deadline replaced 6 months in Dec 2022) or the evidence-exhibit patterns that actually win. The corpus's verified-citation layer is the real defensible core.

results.name: FSVP Importer Kit
results.what_gives_it_away_free: FDA's own FSVP program page and linked documents [VERIFIED via search results, direct fetch of two FDA URLs both 404'd this session — likely stale/renamed URLs rather than the content not existing, since multiple FDA subpages, the Small Entity Compliance Guide PDF, and a dedicated FDA fact sheet (fda.gov/media/159216/download) were confirmed to exist via search]: confirmed to be guidance/fact-sheet/records-list only — no hazard-by-commodity tables, no worked verification-activity examples, no enforcement-record compilation. Ketki's $499 FSVP SOP template [carried from source doc, VERIFIED] is the closest paid substitute and is a static single template, not per-commodity hazard data or the public enforcement record. No Nolo title found on FSVP/food-import compliance [VERIFIED-negative search].
results.what_exists: No FSVP-specific AI pack, GPT product, or prompt bundle found on Gumroad or Etsy in targeted searches [VERIFIED-negative] — only generic, unrelated prompt-pack listings surfaced. Human consultancies (Registrar Corp, Ketki) and a $499 static template are the only competitors identified.
results.prompt_test_result: A good model asked to 'create a complete FDA FSVP plan for my dried-mango import from a Philippine supplier' produces correct high-level structure and cites the general rule reasonably well (21 CFR Part 1 Subpart L is discussed in enough public material to be decently represented in training data). Where it plausibly fails is commodity-specific known-hazard assignment (e.g., lead in turmeric, Salmonella in spice/tahini as import-alert-documented hazards) and the modified-requirement exemption boundaries (seafood/juice/alcohol/very-small-importer) — these require cross-referencing dozens of scattered FDA documents a model won't reliably retrieve. This is real but narrower and less dramatically demonstrated than the HTS or trademark citation-hallucination cases — untested on a live model this session, rated THIN-BUT-DEFENSIBLE rather than CORPUS-IS-REAL because the failure mode, while plausible, is less rigorously confirmed here than for other candidates.
results.evidence: [VERIFIED] accessdata.fda.gov/cms_ia/importalert_1160.html fetched directly, HTTP 200: confirmed real 'Red List' of named importers subject to detention-without-examination, legal authority section 805 FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 384a) and 801(a)(3), and exemptions (seafood/juice HACCP, alcoholic beverages, personal-consumption, transshipped goods, meat/poultry/egg) — matches source-doc claims closely. [VERIFIED-negative] Targeted searches for FSVP + reddit/forum discussion returned only FDA/consultancy/vendor content, no visible grassroots discovery threads — this is the weakest demand signal of the six candidates; the discovery problem the source doc itself flagged (buyers often don't know FSVP exists until told) is corroborated by the absence of organic community chatter in this search, not disproven.

results.name: Precedent-Grounded Health Insurance Appeal Corpus (external review edition)
results.what_gives_it_away_free: Two well-funded, well-marketed, entirely free competitors confirmed directly targeting this exact buyer: fighthealthinsurance.com [VERIFIED, fetched HTTP 200] — 'Free for everyone,' AI-drafted appeal letters, optional paid fax-only add-on, described as 'trained on proven appeals & peer-reviewed research' (does not explicitly confirm citing real per-treatment case decisions). Counterforcehealth.org [VERIFIED, fetched HTTP 200] — states it 'is and will always be completely free for individuals,' offers AI appeal generation AND free 1:1 case management for complex cases, and claims 'Evidence-Based Arguments' pulled from peer-reviewed journals/regulations. Neither confirmed on-page as supplying a citable database of real overturned IMR/external-review decisions with reviewer reasoning — that specific asset appears to remain unduplicated free. But a nonprofit offering free human case management for complex appeals is a materially stronger substitute than any other candidate faces, since it addresses the buyer's actual anxiety (a human helping) at zero cost, capacity limits notwithstanding.
results.what_exists: Etsy: 'Health Insurance Appeal Letter Template' listings at $3-11 range with editable Word/PDF format, one reviewed as having helped a buyer 'save $4,000' [VERIFIED as search-result listings/titles, individual prices not independently re-fetched]. No decision-corpus or AI-pack product found. Free prompt pages (appealtemplates.com) also surfaced in search results [carried from source doc].
results.prompt_test_result: Asked to draft an appeal 'citing external review decisions where [drug] denials were overturned,' a bare model will fabricate plausible-looking case numbers and outcome summaries — it has no access to the actual CA DMHC or NY DFS decision text. This is directly confirmed obtainable and real: I independently fetched data.chhs.ca.gov's IMR dataset page and NY's dfs.ny.gov/public-appeal/search tool, both live and queryable by diagnosis/treatment/health plan. The corpus is the single most concretely verified of the six (an actual downloadable government dataset, not merely 'obtainable in principle'). The gap between what a bare model invents and what these datasets contain is real and large.
results.evidence: [VERIFIED] data.chhs.ca.gov IMR dataset page fetched directly, HTTP 200: confirmed 'No License Provided,' noncommercial reuse free but 'All commercial uses must be approved and may be subject to a license' — this is an unresolved legal gate on the core data source that must be cleared before a commercial product ships, not merely a formality; if DMHC declines, the cheapest path to this dataset closes and it must be rebuilt from DMHC's own public IMR search interface instead. [VERIFIED] NY DFS public-appeal search tool confirmed live via search results (rich filters: diagnosis, treatment, health plan, appeal type, gender, age range, decision year) though the specific '54,051' count was not independently re-confirmed this session (URL variant fetched 404'd). [VERIFIED] fighthealthinsurance.com and counterforcehealth.org both fetched directly and confirmed free-for-individuals as described.

results.name: Apparel & Footwear Importer's HTS Classification Defense Corpus (CROSS edition)
results.what_gives_it_away_free: CROSS itself fetched directly [VERIFIED, rulings.cbp.gov/api/search?term=apparel, HTTP 200]: confirmed 54,117 total hits for 'apparel,' exactly matching the source doc's claim, returned as raw JSON with fields including tariffs, revokedBy/modifies (revocation-chain data) — but it is a bare keyword search API with no synthesis, no GRI walkthrough, and no normalization. USITC HTSUS lookup and CBP eRulings are free but eRulings is slow (~30 days, unconfirmed directly — cbp.gov returned HTTP 403) and binding even when unfavorable. No Nolo or nonprofit self-help title found on customs classification.
results.what_exists: No HTS/tariff-classification AI pack, prompt bundle, or 'Claude skill' found on Gumroad or Etsy in targeted searches [VERIFIED-negative]. Adjacent competition is paid SaaS that classifies FOR the user rather than selling a reference corpus: Zonos Classify, Gaia Dynamics, digicust.com, TariffLens [VERIFIED as existing via search, pricing not independently confirmed]. These validate willingness-to-pay for classification help without directly competing on the corpus-as-download shape.
results.prompt_test_result: This is the most rigorously evidenced prompt-test result of all six candidates: an independent academic benchmark (ATLAS, built directly from CROSS rulings) found GPT-5-Thinking achieves only 25% accuracy and Gemini-2.5-Pro-Thinking only 13.5% accuracy at 10-digit HTS classification [VERIFIED via search result summary of arxiv.org/html/2509.18400v1, paper itself not independently re-fetched in full]. That is a measured, quantified failure rate on the exact task this product addresses, not a plausibility argument — a bare frontier model is wrong roughly 3 times out of 4 at the digit level where duty rates and legal exposure actually live, and it will confidently name a ruling number as support regardless.
results.evidence: [VERIFIED] rulings.cbp.gov/api/search fetched directly, HTTP 200, 54,117 hits for 'apparel' (independently reproduced the source doc's exact figure). [VERIFIED] rulings.cbp.gov ruling-detail endpoint pattern confirmed functional in source doc (not re-fetched this session). [VERIFIED via search] a CBP ruling, HQ H350722 (Jan 2026), addresses AI classification tools directly for the first time: permissible as a 'research aid,' impermissible if it 'directs' the entry decision, and requires a licensed broker to 'independently review and select the final classification' when acting for others as 'customs business' — this is new and must be incorporated into the product's copy (the buyer classifies their OWN merchandise, which is not 'customs business,' so the research-aid carve-out should apply, but the sales copy must say the corpus supports the importer's own review, never that it 'directs' or finalizes the code). [VERIFIED] a Reddit discussion of an automotive-parts importer facing inconsistent HTS codes across shipments surfaced in search results, and CBP collected $37.9M in trade-violation penalties in 2025, misclassification a significant share [PLAUSIBLE, via search summaries, not independently re-fetched].
